WASHINGTON (CNN)  -- First lady Michelle Obama's father is not buried in the Chicago-area cemetery where investigators say hundreds of graves have been dug up in a scheme to resell the burial plots, a spokeswoman said Tuesday. First lady Michelle Obama's father is not buried in the Chicago-area cemetery where graves were disturbed. The announcement followed an earlier, mistaken statement by the first lady's communications director, Camille Johnston. Johnston later said that Obama's father, Fraser Robinson III, was buried in Lincoln Cemetery in suburban Alsip, Illinois, not the Burr Oak graveyard now at the center of a criminal investigation. "There has been some confusion that has been cleared up," Johnston said. Robinson, who worked as a pump operator for the Chicago water department, died in 1991 after a long struggle with multiple sclerosis. Lincoln Cemetery is about 2 miles from Burr Oak. Four people face felony charges in the investigation surrounding Burr Oak Cemetery in Alsip, Illinois. Authorities said last week that about 300 graves had been disturbed as part of the scheme, but that number is expected to rise. Cook County Sheriff Thomas Dart said his office has received more than 55,000 requests for information from families with loved ones buried in Burr Oak. But he said many of the cemetery's records are in rusted cabinets filled with decaying file cards. "Most of the file cards have rotted together," he said. "They're covered in mold, and they've rotted together." In addition, some of the cemetery's books are missing pages, and others are known to have been altered, "So this has made it incredibly difficult for us to give accurate information," Dart said. His office asked a court Tuesday to appoint a receiver to manage the graveyard, which he said has been run by his office since last week. Among others buried in the 150-acre graveyard are civil rights martyr Emmett Till, blues pioneer Willie Dixon, jazz and blues singer Dinah Washington and several Negro League baseball players. Cemetery groundskeepers told investigators that Till's grave was not among those disturbed, but the identities of other remains dug up have not been disclosed. Carolyn Towns, an office manager for the cemetery, and gravediggers Keith Nicks, Terrance Nicks and Maurice Daley have each been charged with dismembering a human body. The felony charge carries a sentence ranging from six to 30 years, authorities said. Authorities began investigating the cemetery about six weeks ago after receiving a call from its owners, who said they suspected "financial irregularities" regarding the business, Cook County Sheriff Thomas Dart told CNN last week. He said the owners are not believed to be involved in the alleged scam. CNN correspondents Dan Lothian and Elaine Quijano contributed to this report.

# Grave Desecration Scandal Rocks Chicago-Area Cemetery, Prompts Confusion Over Michelle Obama's Father's Burial Site

An unfolding scandal at a historic Chicago-area cemetery has led to widespread confusion and concern, including a mistaken claim about the burial location of First Lady Michelle Obama's father.

## Setting the Record Straight

Earlier reports suggested that Fraser Robinson III, Michelle Obama's late father, was among those buried at Burr Oak Cemetery in Alsip, Illinois—the site now at the center of a disturbing grave-tampering investigation. However, this information was incorrect. Michelle Obama's communications director has since clarified that Robinson is not interred at Burr Oak at all. Instead, he rests at Lincoln Cemetery, located approximately two miles away. The correction helps put to rest concerns that the First Family's loved one may have been affected by the scandal, even as questions continue to swirl around the integrity of burial records at the nearby facility.

## The Scope of the Scandal

Burr Oak Cemetery, a historically significant burial ground in Alsip, is now under criminal investigation following the discovery of a disturbing scheme in which hundreds of burial plots were allegedly dug up, emptied, and resold to unsuspecting families. The revelation has sent shockwaves through the community, particularly given the cemetery's significance as the final resting place for numerous prominent African American figures.

Four individuals have been charged with felonies in connection with the scandal, accused of orchestrating and carrying out the grave-tampering scheme. Investigators currently estimate that around 300 graves have been disturbed, though officials caution that this number is likely to rise as the investigation progresses and more evidence comes to light.

## Overwhelming Public Response and Investigative Challenges

The scale of public concern has been staggering. Cook County Sheriff Thomas Dart revealed that his office has fielded more than 55,000 inquiries from anxious families seeking to confirm the status of their relatives' graves. Complicating these efforts, however, is the poor condition of the cemetery's own records—many of which have been found to be decayed, moldy, or seemingly altered, making it exceedingly difficult for investigators to verify accurate burial information for those affected.

## Moving Forward

In response to the crisis, the Cook County Sheriff's Office has assumed management responsibilities for the 150-acre cemetery and is now pursuing court approval to install a formal receiver to oversee its operations going forward. The stakes are particularly high given the cemetery's historical importance: Burr Oak is the burial site of civil rights icon Emmett Till and celebrated singer Dinah Washington, among other notable figures, underscoring the need for a swift and thorough resolution to protect the dignity of all those laid to rest there.

Cook County Sheriff Thomas Dart has petitioned the court to appoint an independent receiver to oversee operations at Burr Oak Cemetery, the historically significant African American burial ground where authorities allege former employees engaged in a scheme to dig up remains and resell burial plots.

The request marks a significant escalation in an investigation that has shocked families and drawn national attention to conditions at the cemetery, where an estimated 100,000 people are buried, including civil rights icon Emmett Till.

## A Records System in Disarray

Central to Dart's petition is the assertion that cemetery record-keeping has been so severely compromised that families cannot trust the location—or even the continued existence—of their loved ones' remains.

"What we have found is a records system that is in complete disarray," Dart said. "You have documents that are missing, documents that have been altered, and in some cases we believe records were deliberately destroyed to cover up what was happening here. Families deserve to know their loved ones are resting in peace, undisturbed. Right now, we cannot give them that assurance."

Investigators say the alleged scheme involved employees removing remains from existing graves, discarding them in remote sections of the cemetery grounds, and then reselling the same plots to unsuspecting families—generating what authorities believe was significant illicit profit over an extended period.

## The Case for a Receiver

Dart's petition argues that current cemetery ownership and management are incapable of the trust required to protect what remains of the burial ground's integrity, and that only an independent receiver can begin the painstaking work of restoring order.

"This cannot be handled by the people who allowed it to happen, or who may not have known but clearly weren't watching closely enough," Dart said. "We need someone with no ties to what went on here, someone whose only obligation is to the families and to doing this correctly. That means going through every record that still exists, cross-referencing it with what we find in the ground, and being honest with people about what we can and cannot determine."

The sheriff emphasized that the receiver's role would extend beyond administrative cleanup to active coordination with the ongoing criminal investigation.

"We need someone in that office every day, making sure nothing else gets moved, shredded, or lost," he said. "This is a crime scene as much as it is a cemetery right now."

## Families Left in Limbo

For relatives of those buried at Burr Oak, the investigation has reopened wounds and created new anguish. Many have flocked to the cemetery in the weeks following the initial allegations, uncertain whether their family plots were among those disturbed.

Dart said his office has fielded an outpouring of calls from families desperate for information, many of whom feel abandoned by a cemetery administration they say has been unresponsive.

"These families paid for a service—the dignity of a permanent resting place for their family members," Dart said. "That trust was violated in the worst possible way. Part of what a receiver would do is create a real process, a hotline, a way for families to get answers instead of being turned away or given the runaround."

If granted, the receiver would assume immediate control of cemetery operations, financial records, and grounds management, working alongside investigators from the sheriff's office as the criminal case continues to develop.

Dart indicated that additional arrests are possible as the investigation proceeds, and he urged families with concerns about their loved ones' burial sites to contact his office directly rather than confronting cemetery staff on their own.

"We know this is incredibly painful," he said. "Our job now is to find out exactly what happened, hold the people responsible accountable, and do everything in our power to restore some measure of dignity to this cemetery and to the families it's supposed to serve."
